summary:
Thüringen is a federal state of Germany. National law on identity documents, legal gender recognition and prison placement applies here as it does elsewhere in the country; the material below is the Thüringen-specific layer.

That layer is configured by the Landtag elected on 1 September 2024. AfD Thüringen took 32.8% of the vote and is classified by the state's Office for the Protection of the Constitution as right-wing extremist. The CDU followed at 23.4%, the BSW at 15.8% in its first state election, Die Linke at 13.1% and the SPD at 6.1%. The CDU, BSW and SPD formed the state's first Brombeer coalition under minister-president Mario Voigt, a minority cabinet without its own Landtag majority. Formal, multi-layered institutional hostility to gender policy in Thüringen rests on this configuration.

Nothing in the sources reviewed documents a trans-specific safety incident, police practice or refusal of service in Thüringen. What is recorded for the state is legislative and party-political, with no state-level enforcement or violence record to assess.
tangentialFactors: On 2 June 2026 Thüringen co-signed an initiative brought by Sachsen and Sachsen-Anhalt to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act. The proposal followed the Liebich case, and its anti-abuse amendments were presented alongside measures for stronger recognition of trans and intersex people. The initiative concerns the federal statute rather than state law; Thüringen's role is a co-signature, not a separate state recognition regime.
localsOnly: The AfD fraction in the Thüringen Landtag has moved that the existing ban on gender-inclusive language in state schools be consistently implemented, arguing in its motion that schools must not be a socio-political experimental field. The same fraction has proposed dismantling the state's equality machinery. These measures bear on residents: pupils, teaching staff and anyone who uses state anti-discrimination structures.
outOfScopeNotes: No source in the inventory records trans-specific violence, policing or prosecution in Thüringen, so no state-level risk assessment of that kind can be made from this material. Whether the co-signed initiative to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act advances, and in what form, is unresolved. The coalition's lack of its own Landtag majority leaves the passage of the school-language measure and the proposed dismantling of the equality machinery open.
